description: Each college's size is the number of player_college records it has (player-years).

b.request: For each `college_id` (NULL grouped as one group), count `player_college` rows; take the mean of those counts across colleges as the threshold; keep colleges whose count is strictly greater; return the mean of their counts, the mean of each count divided by the sum of all counts, and the mean of (count − threshold), unrounded
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS threshold, SUM(cnt) AS total FROM counts), kept AS (SELECT c.cnt FROM counts c, stats s WHERE c.cnt > s.threshold) SELECT AVG(k.cnt) AS mean_count, AVG(1.0 * k.cnt / s.total) AS mean_share, AVG(k.cnt - s.threshold) AS mean_excess FROM kept k, stats s;

a.request: In `player_college`, give each college (by `college_id`, with records lacking a college_id treated as one group) a count equal to its number of records, so every player-year row counts. Find the colleges whose count is strictly above the average count across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) the average count among those colleges; (2) the average of each such college's count divided by the total of the counts summed over all colleges; and (3) the average amount by which their counts exceed the all-college average count. Do not round.
a.sql: WITH college_counts AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM college_counts), above AS (SELECT c.cnt FROM college_counts c CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE c.cnt > s.avg_cnt) SELECT (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM above) AS avg_count_above, (SELECT AVG(a.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt) FROM above a CROSS JOIN stats s) AS avg_share_of_total, (SELECT AVG(a.cnt - s.avg_cnt) FROM above a CROSS JOIN stats s) AS avg_excess_over_mean;

c.request: Using `player_college`, work out each college's player count (by `college_id`, with records lacking a college_id treated as one group). Then find the colleges whose player count is strictly above the average across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) those colleges' average player count; (2) the average of each one's player count as a fraction of the total of all colleges' player counts; and (3) the average amount by which they exceed the all-college average. Do not round. Each college's size is the number of player_college records it has (player-years).
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM counts), above AS (SELECT c.cnt FROM counts c, stats s WHERE c.cnt > s.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(a.cnt) AS avg_above_count, AVG(a.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt) AS avg_fraction_of_total, AVG(a.cnt - s.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_all_college_avg FROM above a, stats s;

d.request:
Rephrased as a standalone question:

Using `player_college`, count the number of `player_college` records for each `college_id` (treating records with no college_id as one group). Then find the colleges whose record count is strictly above the average record count across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) the average record count of those colleges; (2) the average of each of those colleges' record count as a fraction of the total record count across all colleges; and (3) the average amount by which those colleges' record counts exceed the all-college average. Do not round.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_college GROUP BY college_id), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts), total AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM counts), above AS (SELECT c.cnt FROM counts c, avg_c a WHERE c.cnt > a.avg_cnt) SELECT (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM above) AS avg_record_count, (SELECT AVG(1.0 * cnt / (SELECT total_cnt FROM total)) FROM above) AS avg_fraction_of_total, (SELECT AVG(cnt - (SELECT avg_cnt FROM avg_c)) FROM above) AS avg_excess_over_average
